original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: For the alphabet extension of PR1498 (a second arbitrary dirty connector z1 with paid one-way transfer C: z0 += z1, freely chosen source ports), determine the exact minimum number of transfers for the universal five-source batch (all 31 nonzero masks) when every B and A operator is called exactly twice, and price the resulting completed bill against the one-connector repair.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one added operation gives a favorable completed budget. PR1498 already added the transfer operation and left open whether six transfers suffice; the necessary bill cannot be evaluated until the minimum count is known. This refines the card to that exact count; the operation alphabet is unchanged from PR1498 and no source count is increased.
bottleneck_link: A legal extra connector operation could lower recursive interface cost only if its full count and price beat the old repair. Settling the minimum at eight transfers fixes the necessary inequality 8 sigma + Delta H < 2c (equal prices). Side result for the interface catalogue; it does not touch the selected supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the six-transfer census is exhaustive with two independent implementations; if no universal schedule exists, run eight transfers once and stop at the first replayed witness. No search beyond eight transfers or other alphabets.
evidence: Two independent C censuses (prefix formula vs literal two-row simulation, different orbit quotients) agree on all per-split coverage histograms at t=4 (30,270,240 orbits), t=6 (242,161,920 orbits, max 31/32) and t=8 (1,323,241,920 orbits, 2,502 universal). Two eight-transfer witnesses replayed in free noncommutative F2 algebra and dense F2 matrices with 372 rejected mutation controls; predecessor 945-path histogram reproduced against its pinned certificate.
author: nedveder (GitHub)
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Anthropic) assistance for search design, C/Python implementation and write-up.

open_questions.question: Can a hosted transfer satisfy 8 sigma + Delta H < 2c on an actual port pair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the two-connector alphabet can ever beat the 74-call one-connector repair.
open_questions.first_step: Price a two-address row XOR on the selected tape layout, including access, restoration and dispatch.
open_questions.blocked_by: No instance of this multi-output connector interface exists in the selected supplier.

open_questions.question: Do bidirectional transfers (z1 += z0 as well) lower the minimum below eight?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A reverse transfer changes the dirt-phase structure that forces eight one-way transfers.
open_questions.first_step: Add a fourth event stream to native/census_literal.c and rerun t=4 and t=6.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing beyond compute; the census size grows by the extra stream multinomial.

open_questions.question: Is there a short written proof that six one-way transfers fail?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Review would no longer depend on native code for the six-transfer exclusion.
open_questions.first_step: For r=1, split by the even number of transfers inside the z1 window; 0 or 6 give no mixed mask and 2 reduce to the 945-path census.
open_questions.blocked_by: The four-inside case of r=1 and the r=2 split have no written argument yet.
